messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple kubelet restarts detected in infer-west-1 affecting inference-pool-2 (NotReady spikes). Pager routed to oncall.
maya: got paged, joining. seeing elevated 5xxs and latency on hosted API metrics.
jon: I noticed spike in node NotReady count ~10:22 UTC, then kubelet restart logs. some nodes recover, some bounce repeatedly.
srini: opening k8s events + node descr now. might be kernel OOM / cgroup memory pressure.
elena: can we confirm if this is only infer pool? any dedicated/private impact?
maya: only infer-west-1 GPU pool so far. dedicated clusters green.
devon: past incidents similar were driver/GPU oom on cuda 525 causing kubelet to restart due to container runtime thrash. pulling logs.
ops-bot: Command run: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=inference -o wide --context=wc-infer-west1`
jon: nodes: infer-nodex-1..8, three in NotReady. kernel messages show `oom_kill` for containerd-shim and `kubelet: SIGSEGV` during GC.
srini: paste logs: ```
May 29 10:21:44 infer-nodex-3 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 24122 (containerd-shim) total-vm:125g, anon-rss:112g
May 29 10:21:44 infer-nodex-3 kubelet[1234]: runtime panic: invalid memory address
May 29 10:21:45 infer-nodex-3 systemd: kubelet.service: main process exited, code=killed
```
maya: that points to overall memory pressure on node; but why on kubelet? maybe node OOM hit system reserved or kubelet cgroup. Are we running any heavy host-level process?
devon: checking nv-host metrics and pod-level memory. several inference pods using large kv caches (LLM session caching) ramped up. Also noticed a batch job scheduled yesterday bumped up gpu memory usage on same nodes.
ken: support: any customer-facing error messages? receiving a couple of support tickets about timeouts.
maya: yes, some clients saw 504s and aborted streams. severity: S2 for now but could escalate.
srini: mitigation proposals: 1) cordon the 3 flapping nodes 2) drain non-critical pods to reduce pressure 3) scale up new nodes with slightly larger system-reserved memory 4) temporary routing: shift traffic away from infer-west-1 to infer-usw for high-tier customers.
elena: agree on cordon + drain. start scaling pool with new launch template that adjusts kubelet memory/cgroup config?
junior-bot: Note: automated auto-heal tried to replace nodes but kept hitting same image with older driver.
maya: actioning cordon/drain now. @devon can you start node provision with driver 530 and kubelet config bump (system-reserved=2Gi)?
devon: starting ASG scale + new launch config with driver 530 and extra host memory. also will pin lower KV cache size for new nodes via nodeSelector+toleration config.
ops-bot: `kubectl cordon infer-nodex-3` -> OK
ops-bot: `kubectl drain infer-nodex-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` -> in progress
jon: while draining, one node restarted again and reappeared NotReady -> Ready -> NotReady loop. suspect hardware flakiness or out-of-band process.
srini: let's disable auto-scheduler for inference queue to stop scheduling new long-running sessions into these nodes. routing rule updated to deprioritize infer-west-1.
maya: notifying customers about degraded latency for a subset of regions. draft message: "We're investigating increased timeouts for inference in west region; routing and mitigations underway. Will update in 30m." anyone want to edit?
ken: add ETA and mention impacted customers may see 10-30s higher latency, some timeouts.
elena: also escalate to infra-eng for hardware node checks, may need host NIC/firmware inspection.
devon: new nodes coming up with driver 530 and adjusted kubelet flags. once up I'll test by scheduling canary small inference pods.
ops-bot: new node infer-nodex-9 created (IP 10.3.9.12) status: Ready
maya: scheduling canary to infer-nodex-9... logs look good, no kv-cache spikes.
jon: rolling traffic shift now: update router weight to send 70% away from infer-west-1; 30% retained for capacity testing.
srini: monitoring: error rate down from 6% to 1.2% after cordon + new nodes. latency p50 back to 180ms from 420ms.
maya: handoff: I'm staying on for 20 more minutes to ensure stability, then will hand to night oncall. if error rate stays <2% we can demote incident.
devon: note: we should add a safeguard in runtime to limit per-pod KV cache by default to prevent node-level memory exhaustion. filing ticket I-12345.
elena: opening infra ticket to run hardware diagnostics on the three flapping nodes.
ken: support: sending an update to affected customers now.
maya: incident summary draft: "kubelet restarts on several inference nodes caused by node-level OOMs and containerd thrash; root cause appears to be unbounded LLM KV cache + a batch job that increased memory footprint; mitigations: cordon/drain flapping nodes, provision new nodes with updated driver and kubelet system-reserved, temporary routing away from region, and config changes to cap kv cache. Postmortem to follow."
ops-bot: Incident timeline recorded. severity downgraded to S3 at 10:49 UTC.
maya: leaving handoff notes in pager duty and ops-runbook. @srini you own postmortem?
srini: will take PM, collecting logs and creating timeline.
jon: last check: all critical traffic healthy. I'll keep an eye for 1hr then close thread. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks all. closing updates from my side.
ops-bot: This thread will be archived when closed.
